verdict_reason: Tests prove the selected id is carried and replaced through paging links, but a hand-written fixture leaves the radio-only guard unproven and one title over-claims.

todos.issue: The hand-written fixture in render() (lines 11-22) holds only two radios and a pagination nav, but the real form in party-picker/_address-picker.njk:63-80 also holds the q search input (appSubmittedSearch) and hidden inputs. The radio guard in picker-paging-selection.js:20 (if (!target?.matches?.(RADIO_SELECTOR)) return) is never exercised: deleting it leaves all three tests green, yet without it a change in the search box would write the typed text into every paging link's selected param. Sibling component tests (multi-select-search.test.js:27, transporter-filter.test.js:69) render the real template through nunjucksConfig instead.
todos.fix: Must: the tests run against the picker's real markup (or a fixture holding its search input), and one test fails if a change event from a non-radio input rewrites the paging links. One way: render the addressPicker macro with nunjucksConfig's environment as the sibling tests do, then add 'Should leave the paging links alone when the search text changes', which types in #q, dispatches change and asserts the original hrefs.

todos.issue: The title 'Should replace the address the server rendered each time another is ticked' does not state what its assertion proves. The second tick replaces danish-meat-export-aps, the address the first tick wrote, not the server-rendered alpine-dairy; the assertion proves only that the latest tick wins. Replacing the server-rendered address is already what the first test proves.
todos.fix: Must: the title states what the assertions prove: that after several ticks the paging links carry only the address ticked last. One way: rename to 'Should carry only the address ticked last when the trader changes their choice'.
